concepts.title: Counting Iterations of the range Function
concepts.definition: The range(start, stop, step) function generates integers from start up to but excluding stop, moving by step; the number of values it yields equals the span divided by the step, rounded upward, and a negative step walks downwards.
concepts.key_idea: The stop value itself never appears in the generated sequence, and omitting start or step defaults them to 0 and 1.

solution_steps.explain: Subtract the start from the stop to see the ground to cover.

solution_steps.action: round the span up over the step
solution_steps.explain: Adding step minus 1 before floor division rounds the count upward.

concepts.title: Positive Difference with Selection
concepts.definition: An if..else statement picks between two paths, so subtracting the smaller number from the larger always yields a positive difference; equivalently, taking the square root of the squared difference removes the sign.
concepts.key_idea: Whichever branch runs, the same subtraction pair is ordered so the result never goes negative.

solution_steps.explain: The raw difference may be negative.
Squaring then taking the square root leaves the magnitude.

worked_examples.q: One number is 9 and the other is 4. What is their positive difference?

concepts.title: Sum of Digits of an Integer
concepts.definition: A while loop can peel one digit per pass: the remainder on division by 10 is the last digit, floor division by 10 discards it, and the loop adds each peeled digit into a running total until nothing remains.
concepts.key_idea: Modulus 10 captures the current last digit and floor division by 10 shortens the number for the next pass.
concepts.textbook_ref: kecs106.txt, Exercise 7 and Program 6-10 style loops
question_patterns: Find the sum of the digits of 472 using repeated modulus and floor division.

solution_steps.explain: Modulus 10 isolates the final digit.
Floor division by 10 removes the units digit.
The same modulus trick on the shortened number gives the tens digit.
One more floor division leaves the hundreds digit.
Add all three extracted digits.

worked_examples.q: What is the sum of the digits of 472?

concepts.title: Factorial of a Number with a Loop
concepts.definition: The factorial of n multiplies every whole number from 1 up to n; a for loop with range(1, num + 1) folds each value into an accumulator that starts at 1, and negative inputs are refused because no factorial exists there.
concepts.key_idea: The accumulator begins at 1 because multiplying by 1 changes nothing, and the loop visits num values.
question_patterns: Trace the factorial program for input 5 and state the printed result.
Why does the factorial loop use range(1, num + 1) instead of range(1, num)?
What does the factorial program print when the user enters 0, and why?
Compute 6 factorial by hand the way the loop would.
Why is the accumulator initialised to 1 rather than 0?

solution_steps.explain: The loop multiplies num by num minus 1 first.
Each pass multiplies one smaller value.
The accumulator keeps growing.
Multiplying by 1 closes the chain.

concepts.title: Sum of Even Numbers up to N
concepts.definition: A loop that tests num % 2 == 0 prints or adds only the even members of a sequence; up to a limit n there are n // 2 even numbers, and their total is half-count times half-count plus one.
concepts.key_idea: Every second number is even, so the count of evens below n is simply n // 2.

solution_steps.explain: Half of the numbers up to n are even.
Doubling k gives 2, 4, 6, ... and their sum factors as k times k plus 1.

concepts.title: Loop Sum of a Cubed Sequence
concepts.definition: The sequence 1 + 1/8 + 1/27 + ... + 1/n cubed adds one reciprocal of a perfect cube per loop pass; each pass raises the counter to the power 3, divides 1 by it, and folds the term into the total.
concepts.key_idea: Term k of the sequence equals 1 divided by k cubed, so the exponent operator builds every denominator.
question_patterns: Evaluate the sum 1 + 1/8 + 1/27 correct to three decimal places.

solution_steps.explain: Cube the counter 2 and invert it.
Cube the counter 3 and invert it.
The first term is 1, so add the two new terms to it.

worked_examples.q: What is the first term of the series 1 + 1/8 + 1/27 + ...?

concepts.title: Elif Ladder for Grade Allocation
concepts.definition: An if..elif..else chain tests grade boundaries from the top down: above 90 percent earns an A, 80 to 90 a B, 70 to 80 a C, 60 to 70 a D, and anything below lands in the final else block; the first true condition wins and the rest are skipped.
concepts.key_idea: Order matters in an elif ladder: testing the lowest band first would swallow every higher grade.
question_patterns: Which grade does a student with 78 percent receive in the given allocation table?
Write a program that reads a percentage and prints the matching grade A to E.
Why must the condition for grade A be checked before the condition for grade B?

solution_steps.explain: Compare the percentage with each boundary in descending order; the first satisfied condition assigns the grade and skips the remaining tests.

worked_examples.q: In a top-down grade ladder, which letter grade does 95 percent earn when above 90 is an A?

concepts.title: Break and Continue Statements
concepts.definition: The break statement abandons the loop entirely and jumps to the first statement after it, while continue abandons only the current pass and returns to the loop's condition for the next pass.
concepts.formula: break -> exit loop; continue -> next iteration
concepts.key_idea: Break answers 'stop everything', continue answers 'skip this one', and mixing them up changes the output count.
question_patterns: In Program 6-12, which is the last value printed before the break fires, and why?
Why is the value 3 missing from the output of the continue demonstration?
Differentiate break and continue with one example of each.
A while True loop reads numbers and stops at the first negative entry. Which statement ends the reading?
What becomes of the statements after a continue inside the loop body for that pass?

solution_steps.action: trace the loop with the jump in place
solution_steps.explain: Break transfers control past the loop body permanently; continue transfers it back to the loop condition, so the remaining statements of the current pass are skipped only.
